title: Pentagon UAP documents disappoint as White House faces UFO file release distraction claims
excerpt: The Pentagon released a new batch of UAP files on Friday, but many were left underwhelmed by the lackluster photos and videos, with critics calling the UFO file release a distraction from the administration's failings
content:
Jack Hobbs

Fri, September 18, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC

White House officials are under fire for publishing what critics are calling a disappointing UFO report that many believe is merely a smokescreen to divert attention from the administration's shortcomings.

The latest tranche of files was released by the Department of Defense on Friday, featuring 10 separate accounts and images purportedly depicting UFOs. Yet many of the nighttime photographs show little more than tiny dots of light, which could easily be stars or aircraft.

Pentagon chief spokesperson Sean Parnell released a statement alongside the documents. "Today, the Department of War is publishing the sixth release of declassified and historical Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) files as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE)," he said.

• Fans rage at Trump for 'worst release' of UFO files including 'potato in sky' image

• 'China's Nostradamus' issues blunt assessment of Donald Trump's UFO file release

Parnell confirmed that additional documents will be made public on a "rolling basis" via the department's website. "The Department of War and our agency partners are actively working on the next release of UAP files," he added.

Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy talked up the underwhelming release. "I was summoned to an office in the West Wing yesterday for a private briefing about these files that you're about to see on your screen for the first time ever," said Doocy, reports the Irish Star.

"Let's show the first clip. It was taken by a Navy aerial photographer. His name was Delbert Newhouse. It was taken along a Utah highway, he added. " he added. "If you look closely, it looks like a drone swarm, but there were no known drones in the sky when this video was taken in 1952.

"I am told they took the first and only copy of this film. They found it in the National Archives," the Fox News host continued. "It has been digitized into 4K to be released right here for the first time today."

Doocy then screened a second clip, reportedly captured by a Colorado law enforcement officer in 2023. "The officer's narration and some nearby buildings have been redacted," Doocy noted.

The journalist revealed he had listened to the full, unredacted recording, in which the officer described witnessing multiple orbs "hovering over a sensitive military installation for 15 minutes at a time."

Doocy went on to say, "We have a third clip taken by a drone over the Middle East last year. It showed six objects flying in formation, destination unknown.

"Depending on how they look at this, they say they do not know what they're looking at on the screen," he continued. "And then there's this, there's a newly declassified copy of an expense report, a line-by-line expense report."

Doocy revealed the document detailed the $22 million the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) spent investigating a claim surrounding the notorious Skinwalker Ranch, a location long associated with alleged UFO sightings. "Senior White House officials are telling me they cannot find any copy of the records. They've got all the proof that this government contractor was spending $22 million to do this investigation," added Doocy.

"But we should stress, again, officials do not know what the objects are in these videos that are going to go wide online after this report at war.gov slash UFO."

Many X users were quick to dismiss the release as a smokescreen for the Trump administration's controversies. "The white house. Literally anything to distract from all the garbage they're doing," one X user said.

"No one cares, people are concerned about the economy and why Trump forced America into a war on behalf of Israel," another person added. A third person joked that the administration needed to "step it up" and that the file drop was "lame."
